transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you, too. Um, I want to make sure I explain this right, so please just let me know if I'm rambling. 

I guess I'm here because things have been kind of stressful at work lately. I'm a transportation inspector. And, well, I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining or making a big deal out of nothing, because I usually try to get along great with everyone. But ever since I won this county safety award a little while back... certain people at the office have been sort of twisting my inspection reports. They keep asking me these really pointed budget questions, almost like they're trying to make me look crooked? 

And I know my supervisor says it’s just a normal review, and I really try to be a team player and listen to him, but... I can just tell there’s some kind of coordinated effort going on to discredit me. 

Is it okay that I start with that? I hope I'm explaining it in a way that makes sense.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you couldn't hear or see?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. Um... I hope I didn't say anything to make you think I was... you know, imagining things? 

I promise I've never heard voices or seen anything that isn't actually there. I just... I just notice the real things they're doing with my reports at work. I'm completely grounded in reality, I swear. Does that make sense? I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture and not making myself sound, um, crazy or anything.
Have you noticed these same kinds of suspicious behaviors or attempts to discredit you from people outside of your workplace, such as friends, family members, or neighbors?

Oh, no, definitely not. My friends and family are... they're really great. We get along fine. And my neighbors are perfectly nice, too. I always try to be a good neighbor, you know? 

Um, so it's really just that specific group at the office, because of the award and the budget stuff. I really don't want you to think I'm just going around suspecting everyone of things, because I'm honestly not like that at all. I have a very normal, quiet life outside of my job. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for. I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.

Have you ever tried to bring these concerns about your inspection reports to someone outside of your office, such as a union representative or an outside authority, to see if they could confirm that your reports are being tampered with?

Um, no, I haven't done anything like that. I really... I don't want to make a huge fuss or get anyone in actual trouble, you know? 

I try my best to be professional and handle things internally. I feel like if I went to the union or, like, an outside investigator, it might make me look like a difficult employee, and I really pride myself on being easy to work with. I'd hate for them to think I was trying to start a war or something. So I've just been keeping it to myself, mostly, and just trying to do my job the best I can. 

I hope that was the right thing to do? I just really didn't want to blow it out of proportion or make things harder for my supervisor. I hope that makes sense.
What do you believe is the underlying reason or motivation for your coworkers to be acting this way toward you?

Um... honestly, I'm not entirely sure. I don't really know why they would go to this much trouble. I mean, like I mentioned before, I figured it was mostly just about the department award, or maybe some budget stuff where they need to make my inspection numbers look worse so theirs look better? But... I don't really have, like, a big theory about it or anything. 

I try not to sit around thinking about their motives too much, you know? I really want to give everyone the benefit of the doubt. I'm sure they aren't, like, bad people... probably just a little too competitive about the metrics? 

I hope that's an okay answer. I just really don't want to sound like I'm accusing them of some huge, crazy master plan, because I'm definitely not doing that. I'm just trying to do my job and keep my head down. Does that make sense? I really hope I'm explaining this right.
Aside from the stress you've been feeling at work, have you noticed any changes in your mood, energy levels, or your interest in activities you usually enjoy?

Um, no, not really. I mean, obviously the work stuff is a bit draining, but other than that, I feel completely fine. My mood is good, and I still have plenty of energy for my hobbies on the weekends. I still really enjoy going to the gym and hanging out with my friends, so nothing's really changed there. 

I try to keep a really positive attitude, you know? I don't want to let the office stress ruin the rest of my life. I think I'm doing a pretty good job of balancing it all. 

Is that what you mean? I just want to make sure I'm not leaving anything out that you need to know. I'm really trying to give you the best answers I can.
How long have you felt that your coworkers were tampering with your inspection reports?

Um, well... I'd say it's been about a year now. Yeah, right around a year. It started, um, right after I got recognized for that county safety initiative we did. 

I guess maybe that brought a little too much attention to me? I really didn't mean to show anyone up or anything, I was just doing my job. But that seems to be when the, you know, the little discrepancies in my reports started showing up. 

I really hope I don't sound like I'm bragging about the safety initiative thing. I just thought the timing might be helpful for you to know? I'm just trying to give you the exact timeline you asked for. Did I answer that okay?
Do you feel that you have any special talents or have you ever received any other recognition that might explain why people would feel jealous or threatened by you?

Um, no, no, definitely not. I don't have any special talents or anything like that. I'm just a regular guy, really. 

I mean, I'm good at my job, I guess, but that's just because I try to work hard and pay attention to the details. The county safety initiative was nice, but it was just a team effort, you know? I was just doing my part. I haven't gotten any other awards or anything that would make someone jealous. 

I really don't think I'm better than anyone else in the office. I just want to do my inspections and go home. I hope that doesn't make me sound boring or anything? I just... I really don't think there's anything special about me that would make people feel threatened. Does that make sense? I want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking.
When you are speaking, do you ever feel like your thoughts are racing or that you have trouble keeping your ideas organized?

Oh, no, definitely not. My thoughts feel pretty normal to me. I don't ever really feel like my mind is racing or getting all jumbled up. 

I mean, I try really hard to stay focused and keep everything straight, especially with my inspections, and, well, here with you too. I like to take my time and make sure I'm explaining things clearly so I don't give you the wrong idea or waste your time. 

I feel like I'm keeping my ideas pretty organized right now, don't you think? I really hope I'm making sense. I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your notes. Am I doing okay with how I'm answering?
Have you ever felt that your body was changing in a strange way, or that you were experiencing physical sensations that you couldn't explain?

Um, no, nothing like that. My body feels completely normal to me. I mean, I get a little sore sometimes from walking around doing inspections all day, but that's just regular muscle soreness, you know? Nothing strange or unexplained at all. 

I try to take pretty good care of myself and stay healthy. I really hope it's okay that my answer is just a plain no for that one? I don't want to leave anything out if you need it for your evaluation, but I honestly haven't noticed anything weird happening with my body. I'm trying my best to be as helpful as possible. Is it a good sign that I don't have those kinds of issues?
